about: ShopSmart is a mobile-first grocery price-comparison and smart-shopping app for the Canadian market, piloting in Edmonton, AB. It finds the cheapest per-item prices across multiple local stores and then either guides the shopper along an optimized multi-stop driving route with per-store checklists (Drive Mode) or dispatches an Uber Direct driver for curbside multi-stop pickup and home delivery (Delivery Mode). Price data starts crowdsourced from users (GasBuddy-style, with gamified points) and is later supplemented by flyer parsing and retailer partnerships. The repo currently contains the product/build spec, business and technical planning docs, and an interactive HTML screen mockup; the React Native/Expo app and Node/Express backend are specified but not yet implemented.
whyThis: Unlike GasBuddy (fuel only), Flipp (flyer browsing with no routing or delivery), or Instacart and store apps (single-store ordering), ShopSmart pairs true cheapest-per-item comparison across stores with actionable last-mile execution, turning a savings calculation into either an optimized driving route or a single multi-stop delivery. It is the only approach here wiring multi-store grocery optimization to a white-label multi-stop delivery API (Uber Direct), so users capture the savings without personally visiting several stores. It targets acute, timely demand: Canadian food inflation peaked at 9.8% in 2022 and ~70% of Canadians are cutting non-essential spending. Crowdsourced pricing avoids scraping and builds a defensible, community-driven data moat in one local market before expanding.
funding: The business plan does not state a specific raise, so this amount is an estimate derived from its own Year 1 figures: roughly CAD $75k-$150k of pre-seed/seed capital would fund the Year 1 build and Edmonton pilot plus a runway cushion to the projected mid-Year-2 break-even. The plan budgets about $72k of Year 1 cost - roughly $40k to build the Expo/React Native app and Node.js/PostgreSQL backend, plus Uber Direct, Google Maps and cloud infrastructure, about $12k for marketing/user acquisition and $8k for operations - against about $26k of Year 1 pilot revenue, a planned ~$46k net loss. That capital unlocks the Q1 2027 Edmonton iOS launch (Drive Mode, crowdsourced pricing) targeting 1,000 active users, then Delivery Mode via Uber Direct and the $5.99/mo Pro subscription with a 500-subscriber target. On the plan's own projections this reaches about $211k revenue in Year 2 (Alberta + BC expansion, break-even mid-Year-2) and about $1.0M revenue with ~$596k net profit in Year 3 on national rollout; a larger Series A is only contemplated later (2028) if a VC path is pursued. All revenue and profit figures are the founder's forward projections, not committed or historical results.
